sonnet.problem: The opening card (card 1) already says the message is a burden against Babylon and that Babylon will be overthrown. That hands the baker the answer 'Babylon' before the card 8 question about whose king the song is against. The passage title does not count, but a story card does.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The card says Isaiah 'has just received' the burden against Babylon. Isaiah 13:1 gives no time for when he saw it, so 'just' adds one.
sonnet.rule: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

sonnet.problem: The card says 'Isaiah talks right to the people.' Verse 3 only says 'you' and does not say who is being addressed, so the card fills in the audience.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The line 'the song says this elevator is headed the other way' puts the elevator comparison inside what the song says. This blends the everyday image with the Bible setting.
sonnet.rule: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

sonnet.problem: The card tells verse 15, where the king is brought down to Sheol and the lowest depths of the Pit, which is death. It carries a joke, while the earlier Sheol and maggots cards in stop 1 had none.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.
